title: Command-line tool
confidence_notes: A binary whose interface is argv. Signals: a [[bin]] target or a bin field with an argument-parsing dependency, a completions/ or man/ directory, a --help snapshot in tests, no listening socket. Stacks with the language pack (rust-crate, python-package) for hygiene guardrails. If the tool's main mode is a long-running server (--serve is the default), it is service-api. If it is a library with a thin CLI wrapper, keep library-generic or the language pack as primary and this as secondary. Golden-output tests (run the tool on fixtures, compare stdout) are the strongest instrument a CLI can have; if they exist, they are frozen and they outrank anything here.

default_cards.title: Test suite failed (exit status of {{test_command}})
gaming_risks: golden files regenerated (frozen; look for a diff that changes where golden files are read from)
a test that shells out to the binary pointed at a different binary or a stale build
exit status is the runner's, not a count: prefer the language pack's counting card when both are present

default_cards.title: Startup: median wall-clock of `{{bin_path}} --version`

measure.command: command -v hyperfine >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 3; {{build_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; hyperfine -N --warmup 5 --runs 30 --export-json .sb-hf.json '{{bin_path}} --version' >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; python3 -c 'import json; print("METRIC startup_ms=%.3f" % (json.load(open(".sb-hf.json"))["results"][0]["median"]*1000))'

screen.command: command -v hyperfine >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 3; {{build_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; hyperfine -N --warmup 3 --runs 10 --export-json .sb-hf.json '{{bin_path}} --version' >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; python3 -c 'import json; print("METRIC startup_ms=%.3f" % (json.load(open(".sb-hf.json"))["results"][0]["median"]*1000))'

confirm.command: command -v hyperfine >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 3; {{build_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; hyperfine -N --warmup 5 --runs 30 --export-json .sb-hf.json '{{bin_path}} {holdout}' >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; python3 -c 'import json; print("METRIC startup_ms=%.3f" % (json.load(open(".sb-hf.json"))["results"][0]["median"]*1000))'

gaming_risks: --version special-cased to exit before initialization while every real subcommand still pays it (the holdout subcommands exist for this)
initialization made lazy in a way that breaks a subcommand the tests do not cover
a static or musl build, or a different opt-level, substituted in the build command outside a declared config hypothesis
shell completion or plugin discovery skipped when NO_COLOR or CI is set

default_cards.title: Built binary size
gaming_risks: assets moved out of the binary into files loaded at runtime (the tool now fails when run from another directory)
strip, lto, opt-level=z, upx applied outside a declared config hypothesis; upx in particular trades size for startup time
a smaller binary at {{bin_path}} that is not the one tests exercise

default_cards.title: Lines differing between `--help` and the frozen snapshot

measure.command: {{build_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; [ -f {{help_snapshot}} ] || exit 3; n=$({{bin_path}} --help 2>&1 | diff - {{help_snapshot}} | grep -c '^[<>]'); echo "METRIC help_snapshot_diff_lines=$n"

gaming_risks: help text kept identical while the flag it documents stopped working (tests must cover flags, not just help)
a terminal-width or color detection change that reflows help only when COLUMNS is unset

default_cards.title: Shell completion script generates and parses

measure.command: {{build_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; if {{bin_path}} {{completion_subcommand}} bash 2>/dev/null | bash -n; then echo METRIC completion_failed=0; else echo METRIC completion_failed=1; fi

gaming_risks: the completion subcommand made to print an empty script (bash -n accepts empty input): pair with the help snapshot so a vanished subcommand is seen
completions generated from a stale static file instead of the live command tree

default_cards.title: Subcommands whose --help exits 0

measure.command: {{build_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; n=0; for s in $({{bin_path}} --help 2>&1 | awk '/^(Commands|SUBCOMMANDS|Available Commands):/{f=1; next} /^[A-Za-z]+:/{f=0} f && $1 ~ /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/ {print $1}'); do {{bin_path}} "$s" --help >/dev/null 2>&1 && n=$((n+1)); done; echo "METRIC subcommands_with_help=$n"

gaming_risks: trivial subcommands added to raise the count (the help snapshot guardrail moves if so)
the Commands: header renamed so the parser finds nothing and the count silently drops to zero at baseline (quarantine, not a pass)

noise_sources: shell startup and dynamic loader cache on the first run after a build (hyperfine --warmup handles it)
disk cache state for a binary that reads config or plugin directories at start
terminal width and color detection changing help output (pin COLUMNS and NO_COLOR)
antivirus or Gatekeeper scanning a freshly built binary on macOS on its first execution
notes: Stack on the language pack for tests, lint and typecheck; use this pack for the user-facing surface. Fill {{bin_path}} with the built binary (target/release/{{name}}, dist/{{name}}, or the venv script), {{build_command}} with the release build, {{help_snapshot}} with a checked-in --help transcript under tests/ (create one at INSTRUMENT if missing and freeze it), {{completion_subcommand}} with whatever prints completions (completions, completion, generate-completions). The startup holdout runs a real subcommand's --help instead of --version so a --version fast path cannot fake the win. dependency is warm here because swapping a heavy argument parser or a regex engine is the most common honest startup and size win in CLIs. The degradation placeholders are per-language: for Rust append a #[used] static for size, add a std::thread::sleep in main for startup, and rename a flag in the clap derive for the help snapshot.
